facts.value: Judaism is the oldest Abrahamic religion, originating in the people of ancient Israel and Judah.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: The Torah is its foundational text, and is part of the larger text known as the Tanakh or Hebrew Bible.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Judaism is supplemented by oral tradition, set down in written form in later texts such as the Midrash and the Talmud.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Judaism includes a wide corpus of texts, practices, theological positions, and forms of organization.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Within Judaism there are a variety of movements, most of which emerged from Rabbinic Judaism.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Rabbinic Judaism holds that God revealed his laws and commandments to Moses on Mount Sinai in the form of both the Written and Oral Torah.

facts.value: The Jewish people were scattered after the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem in 70 CE.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Today there are about 13 million Jews, about 40 percent living in Israel and 40 percent in the United States.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: The largest Jewish religious movements are Orthodox Judaism (Haredi Judaism and Modern Orthodox Judaism), Conservative Judaism, and Reform Judaism.
